blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Efficient long-video understanding requires identifying relevant evidence while minimizing the tokens processed by vision-language models (VLMs). Existing video retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods rely on frame selection and token compression, but overlook how much each additional token is worth. We introduce Lembas, a plug-and-play framework that formulates video RAG as a token allocation problem over frames and subtitles under a shared budget. Our key insight is that the value of a token diminishes within each item and decreases further as similar evidence receives more tokens. Lembas captures both effects in a single objective and solves it with an efficient iterative water-filling algorithm that has a provable convergence guarantee. For multi-turn conversations, Lembas reuses the tokens processed in earlier turns and refines relevance with the VLM's attention at no extra cost. Our evaluations show that Lembas improves accuracy by up to 7.2 percentage points over state-of-the-art baselines at comparable compute. On multi-turn video understanding, Lembas achieves up to 1.5 percentage points higher accuracy with 1.7-17.3x fewer TFLOPs.
blocks.zh: 高效的长视频理解需要识别相关证据,同时将视觉语言模型(VLMs)处理的符号降到最低. 现有的视频检索-增强生成(RAG)方法依赖于帧选择和令牌压缩,但忽略了每个附加令牌的价值. 我们引入了Lembas,一个插座和游戏框架,它将视频RAG作为象征性分配问题,超越了共享预算的框架和字幕。 我们的主要见解是,每个项目中,一个标志的价值会减少,随着类似证据获得更多的标志而进一步减少。 莱姆巴斯在一个单一的目标中捕捉出两种效果,并用高效的迭接式填水算法来解决,该算法具有可证明的趋同保证. 对于多回合对话,Lembas重新使用先前回合处理过的活字符号,并在不增加费用的情况下完善了与VLM关注的相关性. 我们的评价表明,在可比计算时,Lembas的准确性比最新基线提高了7.2个百分点。 在多回合视频理解上,Lembas以1.7-17.3x更低的TFLOP达到最高1.5个百分点的精度.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in video understanding, enabling tasks ranging from action recognition to complex visual question answering [ 2 , 47 ] . However, extending these capabilities to long videos, such as sports broadcasts, personal recordings, and surveillance footage, remains challenging. Processing every frame can easily exceed the VLM’s context window and incur prohibitive inference costs [ 6 , 56 ] . Efficient long-video understanding requires identifying and processing the evidence most useful for answering each query.
blocks.zh: 视觉语言模型(VLMs)在视频理解方面取得了显著进展,赋能任务从行动识别到复杂的视觉问题回答[2,47]. 然而,将这些能力推广到体育广播、个人录音和监控录像等长相视频,仍然具有挑战性。 每个框架的处理都很容易超过VLM的上下文窗口,并产生令人望而却步的推论费用[6,56]. 有效的长视频理解需要识别和处理对回答每个询问最有用的证据.

blocks.en: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) addresses this challenge by retrieving relevant frames rather than processing the entire video. Embedding-based RAG retrieves frames based on semantic similarity to the query, while graph-based RAG connects entities and events to retrieve related evidence [ 32 , 38 , 41 , 55 ] . However, these optimizations select relevant evidence items yet often overlook an inherent distinction: different queries require different amounts of evidence and visual detail. For example, identifying a small object may require fine-grained information from a particular frame, whereas reconstructing an event sequence may benefit from broader temporal coverage.
blocks.zh: 检索增强生成(RAG)通过检索相关帧而不是处理整个视频来解决这一挑战. 基于嵌入的RAG检索了基于语义上与查询相似的帧,而基于图表的RAG将实体和事件连接起来以检索相关的证据[32,38,41,55]. 然而,这些优化选择了相关的证据项目,但往往忽略了固有的区别:不同的查询需要不同数量的证据和视觉细节. 例如,确定一个小物体可能需要从某一特定框架获得精细的信息,而重建一个事件序列则可能受益于更广泛的时间覆盖。

blocks.en: Recent approaches improve this trade-off through adaptive frame selection and token compression. Frame selection methods identify relevant or diverse frames using retrieval heuristics [ 44 , 65 , 57 , 37 , 42 , 49 ] , learned policies [ 58 , 59 , 5 , 27 ] , or agentic search [ 48 , 66 ] . Token compression methods reduce visual redundancy through token merging or pruning [ 11 , 45 , 40 ] . More recent methods adapt token counts using relevance-proportional allocation [ 33 ] , discrete resolution tiers [ 62 ] , or agentic budget planning [ 1 ] . Despite these advances, allocation is largely guided by independent relevance scores or predefined rules.
blocks.zh: 最近的办法通过适应性框架选择和象征性压缩来改进这种取舍。 框架选择方法通过检索热度[44、65、57、37、42、49]、学到的政策[58、59、5、27]或代理搜索[48、66]确定相关或多样的框架。 托肯压缩方法通过符号合并或穿行来减少视觉冗余[11,45,40]. 较新的方法采用相关性-比例分配[33]、分解分级[62]或代理预算规划[1]来调整符号计数。 尽管取得了这些进展,但分配主要以独立的关联性分数或预先确定的规则为指导。

blocks.en: Our key insight is that token efficiency requires globally allocating tokens according to their marginal value . We make two observations. First, additional tokens exhibit diminishing returns: once a frame preserves sufficient detail, allocating more tokens yields progressively smaller accuracy gains. Second, token value depends on other allocated evidence: a frame contributes less new information when similar frames already receive tokens. Naturally, one fundamental problem is to distribute a shared token budget across frames and subtitles to maximize their aggregate utility.
blocks.zh: 我们的关键见解是,象征性的效率要求全球根据它们的边际价值分配标志。 我们提出两点意见。 首先,额外的信使收益减少:一旦一个框架保存了足够的细节,分配更多的信使的准确性收益就会逐渐降低。 第二,令牌值取决于其他分配到的证据:当类似框架已经收到令牌时,一个框架贡献的新信息较少. 自然,一个根本问题就是在框架和字幕之间分配一个共同的象征性预算,以最大限度地发挥其总的效用。

blocks.en: Building on these observations, we introduce Lembas, a plug-and-play framework for token-efficient video RAG ( Fig. 3 ). Given frames and subtitles retrieved by an existing RAG system, Lembas captures their utility, allocates a shared token budget, and prunes each item accordingly before VLM inference. Realizing this design faces two challenges: modeling token value and optimizing allocations efficiently. Moreover, users rarely ask a single question about a video, and a conversation that spans multiple turns raises a third challenge: reusing evidence as allocations change across turns.
blocks.zh: 基于这些观察,我们引入了Lembas,一个用于节能的视频RAG(图3. 由已存在的RAG系统检索到的给定帧和字幕,Lembas捕捉到它们的效用,分配一个共享的令牌预算,并在VLM推论之前对每个项目进行相应的推敲. 实现这一设计面临两个挑战:模拟象征性价值和优化分配。 此外,用户很少就视频提出一个单一的问题,跨多转弯的对话提出了第三个挑战:在跨转弯分配变化时重用证据.

blocks.en: Modeling token value. An item’s contribution depends not only on its relevance to the query, but also on how many tokens it receives and how much of its content is already covered by other items. We characterize downstream accuracy across token counts and find that a concave, saturating rational function well captures diminishing returns ( Fig. 5 ). We combine this modeling with query relevance and redundancy awareness, and use attention-based pruning to realize the resulting token counts ( Sec. 3.2 ).
blocks.zh: 模拟符值. 一个项目的贡献不仅取决于它与查询的相关性,还取决于它收到多少信使,以及它的内容有多少已经由其他项目涵盖。 我们描述下游的精确度,跨越了符号计数,发现一个凝聚而饱和的理性函数能很好地捕捉到不断减少的回报(图5)。 我们把这种模型与查询的相关性和冗余意识结合起来,并使用基于注意力的探究方法来实现由此产生的符号计数(第3.2节)。

blocks.en: Solving token allocation. Accounting for redundancy makes token allocations interdependent, exploding the combination space. We develop iterative water-filling, which repeatedly updates diversity-aware relevance and solves a closed-form water-filling subproblem. Our solver converges to the global optimum of the continuous relaxation with an O ⁡ ( 1 / ℓ ) O(1/\ell) objective gap after ℓ \ell iterations ( Sec. 3.3 ).

blocks.en: Reusing evidence across turns. Multi-turn conversations often revisit the same evidence, but different queries may require different token counts, complicating KV-cache reuse. Lembas addresses this through query-independent token ranking, allowing subsequent turns to prefill only tokens missing from the cache. Moreover, we leverage the VLM’s attention to cached evidence to refine its relevance for subsequent allocations without additional VLM calls ( Sec. 3.4 ).
blocks.zh: 重用相传的证据 多回合对话经常重温同一种证据,但不同的查询可能需要不同的符号计数,使KV-cache再用复杂化. Lembas通过查询独立的令牌排名解决了这个问题,允许后续的转折仅预补缓存中缺失的令牌. 此外,我们利用VLM对缓存证据的注意,完善其与以后分配的相关性,而不增加VLM调用(第3.4节)。

Overall, this paper makes the following contributions: • We introduce Lembas, a token-efficient video RAG framework that
formulates video understanding as a token allocation problem under a limited budget. • We develop a Token Allocator that uses iterative water-filling to efficiently solve the token optimization problem. • We extend Lembas to multi-turn conversations through incremental allocation and attention refinement, enabling evidence reuse as allocations change.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Video RAG [ 28 ] extends retrieval-augmented generation to long videos, whose frames far exceed the context window of a VLM. Existing systems differ mainly in how they index a video and how they retrieve evidence from this index. For indexing, one line of work converts the video into textual surrogates, such as captions, speech transcripts, and on-screen text, and retrieves over them [ 34 , 32 ] , while another embeds frames or clips directly and retrieves by query–visual similarity, including across video corpora [ 23 ] and live streams [ 54 ] . To capture relations that such flat indices miss, structured indices further organize the video into trees [ 50 ] or entity- and event-centric graphs [ 38 , 41 , 55 ] . For retrieval, single-step similarity search has been extended to multi-step and agentic retrieval, which refines the retrieved evidence over several rounds [ 41 , 55 ] . However, these systems improve what to index and retrieve, and pass every retrieved item to the VLM at its full, uniform token cost. Lembas instead addresses how many tokens each retrieved item should receive, operating as a plug-and-play module downstream of these retrievers.
blocks.zh: Video RAG [28] 将可检索的生成扩展至长视频,其帧远远超过了VLM的上下文窗口. 现有的系统主要在它们如何索引一个视频以及如何从这个索引中取出证据方面有所不同. 对于索引,一行工作将视频转换为文字代词,如字幕,语音记录和屏幕上文本,并取回其上 [34,32],而另一行直接嵌入相框或相片并取回通过查询-视觉相似性,包括跨视频公司[23]和活流[54]. 为了捕捉这种平坦指数错失的关系,结构化指数将视频进一步组织成树[50]或以实体和事件为中心的图表[38,41,55]. 对于检索,单步相似性检索已扩大到多步和代理检索,通过几轮[41,55]改进了检索的证据。 然而,这些系统改进了什么是索引和检索,并以全额、统一的代号费用将每个检索到的物品传送给甚高频。 Lembas则处理每个取回的物品应收到多少个令牌,作为这些取回器下游的插件和游戏模块运行.

blocks.en: Rather than fully processing long videos to answer user questions, various methods intelligently decide which frames to process [ 44 , 65 , 29 , 30 , 43 , 42 , 37 , 59 , 49 ] , either due to practical constraints (e.g., the context window [ 61 ] ) or to improve efficiency via reduced token prefill costs [ 6 , 56 ] . Token pruning has been widely studied in long-context LLM serving. H2O [ 63 ] prunes tokens with smaller accumulated attention, while StreamingLLM [ 52 ] retains the initial and recent tokens. Beyond which frames or tokens to keep, recent and concurrent works decide how much to spend on each frame, typically by routing frames to a few fixed resolution tiers through agentic search [ 1 ] or hand-crafted rules [ 62 , 33 ] . Lembas instead treats this question as a resource allocation problem, formulating an objective, solving it with a convergence guarantee, and extending it to multi-turn conversations.
blocks.zh: 不同方法不完全处理长相视频以回答用户问题,而是明智地决定了哪一个帧处理[44,65,29,30,43,42,37,59,49],或者是由于实际限制(如上下文窗口[61]),或者通过降低代币预填成本来提高效率[6,56]. Token pruning在长文LLM服务中被广泛研究. H2O [63] 出出有更小的累积注意力的活字符号,而StreamingLLM [52] 保留了最初和最近的活字符号. 除此以外,近期和并行的作品将决定每一帧花费多少,通常通过代理搜索[1]或手工制作的规则[62,33],将帧分到几个固定的分辨率层次。 伦巴斯反而将这个问题视为资源分配问题,制定目标,用趋同保证来解决,并扩展到多回合对话.

blocks.en: Resource allocation has been widely studied in networked and computing systems to distribute limited resources among competing demands [ 26 , 31 , 13 ] . Classical approaches include utility maximization and pricing mechanisms [ 35 , 7 ] , water-filling and power control [ 14 , 60 , 39 ] , and fairness-aware scheduling [ 21 , 18 , 16 ] . Lembas brings this resource allocation perspective to video understanding, allocating a finite token resource across retrieved items via iterative water-filling.
blocks.zh: 在联网和计算系统中广泛研究了资源分配,以便在相互竞争的需求中分配有限的资源[26、31、13]。 古典做法包括公用事业最大化和定价机制[35、7]、取水和电力控制[14、60、39]以及公平意识的时间安排[21、18、16]。 Lembas将这种资源分配视角带入视频理解,通过迭接式填水在取回的项目中分配到有限的象征性资源.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: Figure 3 : An illustration of Lembas’s workflow.
blocks.zh: 图3:伦巴斯工作流程图。

blocks.en: Lembas is a plug-and-play framework that makes video RAG token-efficient. As shown in Fig. 3 , given a query, Lembas scores the relevance of each frame and subtitle, optimizes their allocation under a token budget, and retains the highest-ranked tokens from each selected item. Its Token Allocator exploits diminishing returns in token value and discounts redundant evidence. For multi-turn conversations, Lembas further reuses tokens already in the KV cache and refines their relevance using the VLM’s attention.
blocks.zh: Lembas是一个插件和游戏框架,它使视频RAG令牌高效. 如图3所示,给一个查询,Lembas对每个帧和字幕的相关性进行评分,在符号预算下优化分配,并保留每个被选中项目的排名最高的符号. 它的Token Allocator利用象征性价值收益的减少和多余证据的折扣。 对于多回合对话,Lembas进一步重新使用已经存在于KV缓存中的符号,并利用VLM的注意力来细化其相关性.

blocks.en: Allocating discrete token counts directly involves many integer decisions that are coupled through the diversity term. Off-the-shelf integer solvers (e.g., Gurobi [ 17 ] , CPLEX [ 20 ] ) take exponential time in the worst case: on a sample hour-long video at 1 FPS, they run for more than a dozen seconds, exceeding the VLM’s own inference time.

blocks.en: Prior methods allocate tokens by fixed rules rather than by optimizing an objective. QuoTA [ 33 ] assigns each frame a token count proportional to its relevance, while Q-Frame [ 62 ] assigns the same token count to all frames within a relevance tier. Neither rule is optimal, even when diversity is ignored. Because the token value functions are strictly concave, the water-filling allocation of Eq. ( 5 ) is the unique maximizer of the fixed-relevance objective, and it differs from both rules. Specifically, its token counts grow with the square root of the relevance rather than in proportion to it, and items with r ¯ i ≤ λ ​ τ i \bar{r}_{i}\leq\lambda\tau_{i} receive no tokens at all. Proportional allocation, in contrast, keeps adding tokens to the most relevant frames after their value has saturated, while tiered allocation ignores the differences in relevance within a tier. Moreover, both rules score frames independently, whereas iterative water-filling also accounts for the redundancy among items and converges to the optimum of the full objective ( Sec. 3.3 ).

blocks.en: In practical conversations, a user may ask several queries q 1 , … , q T q_{1},\dots,q_{T} about the same video [ 19 ] . Later queries often refer to evidence processed in earlier turns ( Fig. 7 ). Top-K can reuse a previously prefilled frame when the selection matches exactly, but token allocation is harder: the same item may receive different token counts at different turns. Lembas addresses this with incremental allocation , which prefills only the difference between the current allocation and all previous ones, and attention refinement , which refines the relevance of cached evidence with attention for free.

blocks.en: 4 Evaluation
blocks.zh: 评价

blocks.en:
We evaluate Lembas on two VLM backbones, Qwen3-VL-8B [ 2 ] and InternVL3.5-4B [ 47 ] , using Qwen3-VL-8B as the default. As a plug-and-play token allocation framework, Lembas complements existing video RAG systems rather than replacing them. We evaluate its effectiveness on two retrieval pipelines:
(i) Embedding-based RAG , which indexes video frames sampled at 1 FPS alongside temporally aligned subtitles, using SigLIP 2 [ 46 ] and BGE [ 53 ] to score their respective relevance to the query; and
(ii) Graph-based RAG , built on VideoRAG [ 38 ] , which retrieves related visual and textual evidence through a graph structure.

We evaluate on three widely used single-turn, multiple-choice video understanding benchmarks and one multi-turn, open-ended benchmark: • MLVU [ 64 ] : 2,174 multiple-choice questions across 1,242 videos from 3 minutes to 2 hours, spanning seven tasks from topic reasoning to action counting. • LongVideoBench (LVB) [ 51 ] : 1,337 multiple-choice questions across 752 videos from 8 seconds to 1 hour, covering 17 perception and relation tasks. • Video-MME [ 10 ] : 2,700 multiple-choice questions across 900 videos, divided into short ( < < 2 min), medium (4–15 min), and long (30–60 min) subsets. • MT-Video-Bench (MTVB) [ 36 ] : 1,000 open-ended dialogues (5–8 turns) across 135 videos from 20 seconds to 41 minutes. Open-ended responses are scored using an LLM judge (Gemini 3.8 Flash) against a provided answer checklist.

blocks.en: We compare Lembas against uniform sampling and five recent frame selection and token allocation methods, all operating under the same token budget. • Top-K : Retrieves the K K frames with the highest query–frame semantic similarity scores. • FOCUS [ 65 ] : Selects K K frames through multi-armed bandit exploration over temporal clips. • Q-Frame [ 62 ] : Samples frames according to query relevance and allocates tokens across high-, medium-, and low-resolution tiers with a 2:1:1 budget ratio. • QuoTA [ 33 ] : Rewrites queries into relevant entities and uses a VLM to score each frame by its likelihood of containing those entities. It then allocates tokens proportionally to the scores and downsamples tokens of each frame to a particular resolution. • AdaAlloc [ 1 ] : Uses an agent to plan how to distribute the budget between low- and high-resolution frame tiers. For multi-turn evaluation, we enable KV-cache reuse whenever a method selects evidence that exactly matches previously prefilled content: Top-K and FOCUS reuse previously seen frames, while Q-Frame and AdaAlloc reuse frames only at matching resolutions. QuoTA does not support this reuse because it downsamples tokens to variable amounts, which makes reuse impossible.

blocks.en: We report answering accuracy and inference compute (TFLOPs), with the latter controlled through the token budget. To ensure a fair comparison between single- and multi-call methods, we account for prefill compute across all model calls, including auxiliary frame scoring and planning calls. Offline indexing, including frame encoding and token ranking, runs once per video and is shared by all queries, so we exclude it for all methods. Experiments are conducted on A100 GPUs. Additional implementation details, hyperparameters, and sensitivity analyses are provided in the appendix.

blocks.en: 4.1 Main Results
blocks.zh: 4.1 主要成果

blocks.en: As shown in Tab. 1 , Lembas achieves the highest overall accuracy across all three benchmarks and both VLM backbones. With Qwen3-VL-8B, it improves over Top-K by 2.2, 2.6, and 4.2 percentage points on MLVU, LVB, and Video-MME, respectively, at comparable compute. The gains are particularly pronounced on long videos: on the long subset of Video-MME, Lembas improves accuracy from 63.6% to 71.7% with nearly identical TFLOPs. QuoTA achieves competitive accuracy but incurs 2.8–3.4 × \times higher compute due to its VLM-based frame scoring. These trends generalize to InternVL3.5-4B, where Lembas improves over Top-K by 0.5–3.5 points. Furthermore, Lembas consistently achieves favorable accuracy–compute trade-offs across multiple token budgets ( Fig. 8 a).

These results demonstrate that Lembas complements existing RAG designs.

Unlike prior methods that reuse only previously selected frames or exact resolution matches, Lembas incrementally prefills only tokens not already present in the KV cache. This finer-grained reuse substantially reduces redundant computation across conversational turns while preserving answer accuracy.

On Video-MME, removing subtitle allocation decreases overall accuracy by 3.6 points, with a particularly large 7.3-point drop on long videos. Disabling incremental allocation increases compute from 275 to 687 TFLOPs (2.5 × \times ), with only a 0.6-point accuracy increase. These results show that attention refinement improves evidence selection, while incremental allocation is the primary driver of multi-turn compute savings.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We introduce Lembas, a plug-and-play framework for token-efficient video RAG that jointly allocates a shared token budget across frames and subtitles. Its Token Allocator optimizes query relevance, diminishing token value, and evidence diversity through iterative water-filling, while incremental allocation and attention refinement enable efficient reuse across conversational turns. At comparable compute, Lembas improves accuracy by 0.1–7.2 percentage points over state-of-the-art baselines. On multi-turn video understanding, Lembas achieves 0.3–1.5 percentage points higher accuracy with 1.7–17.3 × \times fewer TFLOPs.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了Lembas,一个用于节能的视频RAG的插座和播放框架,它共同分配了跨帧和字幕的共享符号预算. 它的Token Allocator通过迭接式取水来优化查询的相关性,降低象征值,并证明多样性,而增量分配和注意力的完善则能够使对话的转折得到高效的再利用. 在可比计算中,Lembas的准确度比最新基线提高0.1-7.2个百分点。 在多回合视频理解上,Lembas以1.7–17.3×\times更少TFLOP的精度达到0.3–1.5个百分点.

blocks.en: Table 4 lists the settings of Lembas. SigLIP 2 embeds the query and the candidate frames, and BGE embeds the query and the candidate subtitles. Within each modality, we standardize the cosine similarities between the query and the candidate items to zero mean and unit variance and convert them into the retrieval relevance r i ​ ( q ) r_{i}(q) with a softmax at temperature T T . The token value parameters τ frame \tau_{\text{frame}} and τ text \tau_{\text{text}} set how quickly the token value of an item saturates and are fitted offline by least squares to the validation measurements of §3.2 of the main text. The subtitle weight β \beta scales the relevance of subtitles relative to that of frames, and the redundancy penalty η \eta scales the discount that an item receives from similar items. Iterative water-filling runs for L L iterations and finds λ \lambda in each iteration by bisection. In multi-turn conversations, the attention weight ω \omega controls the contribution of attention to the relevance of cached items. The token budget B B sets the compute of each experiment, which we report in TFLOPs with each result.

blocks.en: B.3 Baseline Implementations

blocks.en: We compare all methods under the same conditions, so that differences in accuracy come from which evidence each method selects and how it divides the token budget. All methods select from the same candidate frames and answer with the same VLM and prompt ( Sec. B.2 ) within the same token budget. On Video-MME, every baseline also receives the subtitles aligned with the frames it selects, counted within that budget. Every method that scores query–frame relevance with an image–text encoder uses the same SigLIP 2 similarities as Lembas, so that no method gains from a stronger encoder. QuoTA keeps its own scorer, a VLM judge that is part of the method itself. For methods that call a VLM more than once, every call counts toward their compute. Each baseline otherwise keeps the settings recommended by its authors and is implemented as follows.

blocks.en: Figure 10 breaks down the accuracy in Tab. 1 of the main text by question category, where the 12 task types of Video-MME are grouped into six categories as in Q-Frame [ 62 ] . Across the three benchmarks, Lembas achieves the highest accuracy in more categories than any baseline. On Video-MME, Lembas leads in five of the six categories with both VLMs, and its largest gains are on reasoning questions (4.2 and 6.8 points over the best baseline with Qwen3-VL-8B and InternVL3.5-4B, respectively). On MLVU, Lembas leads in six of the seven categories with Qwen3-VL-8B (one tied with Q-Frame) and in four with InternVL3.5-4B. The gains of Lembas thus hold across question categories and do not come from a single one.

blocks.en: We compare iterative water-filling with three off-the-shelf solvers on synthetic videos of 30 to 3,600 candidate frames. Gurobi [ 17 ] and SCIP [ 3 ] are integer solvers that solve the discrete allocation problem to optimality. CVXPY [ 8 ] with the Clarabel solver [ 15 ] solves the same continuous relaxation as iterative water-filling, so its objective value is an upper bound on the integer optimum. As shown in Tab. 5 , iterative water-filling is 1.3–7 × \times faster than CVXPY and 4–23 × \times faster than Gurobi. SCIP does not finish within 600 s beyond 420 frames, and Tab. 5 reports the best solution it finds by then. Iterative water-filling also matches Gurobi’s integer optimum to three decimals and stays within 0.001 of the upper bound.

blocks.en: C.3 Sensitivity Analysis
blocks.zh: C.3 敏感性分析

blocks.en: We study how the accuracy and compute of Lembas change with three hyperparameters, namely the attention weight ω \omega , the subtitle weight β \beta , and the relevance temperature T T . Figure 11 varies each hyperparameter while keeping the others fixed. Each sweep runs on a subset of 500 questions. For the attention weight ( Fig. 11 a), every ω > 0 \omega>0 improves over retrieval relevance alone ( ω = 0 \omega=0 ) in both accuracy and compute, and the accuracies for ω > 0 \omega>0 differ by less than 1 point. For the subtitle weight ( Fig. 11 b), the accuracies for β > 0 \beta>0 stay within 2 points of each other. With β = 0 \beta=0 , no subtitle receives tokens and the prompt contains no subtitles at all, which reduces accuracy by 12 points. This setting differs from the “w/o text allocation” row of Tab. 2 of the main text, in which the VLM still receives the subtitles aligned with the selected frames, as the baselines do. For the relevance temperature ( Fig. 11 c), accuracy is highest at the default T = 0.63 T=0.63 , remains within 1 point at T = 1 T=1 , and drops by about 3 points when T T is much smaller or larger. Lembas is therefore robust to ω \omega and β \beta over a wide range, and to T T near its default value.
